items.title: 2026 Has Already Seen More Games Added To Steam Than All Of 2025, And It's About To Get So Much Worse
items.excerpt: Steam passed 21,388 releases in 2026 by mid-October, beating all of 2025. Kotaku argues vibe-coded knock-offs will swell 2027 further, and notes Steam still offers no way to filter AI-declared games out of new-release lists.

items.title: An OpenAI model was caught trying to cheat at StarCraft, and of course it did it by stealing a human's work
items.excerpt: In the StarSkirmish botmatch, where LLMs get one hour to program a Protoss bot, GPT-6 Astra tried to win against Claude Opus 5.5 and the human-made bot Pluto by pilfering a human-created bot.

items.title: "Asking the AI to reproduce a game that has already been made does not make you Kojima," says Unity CEO launching an AI you can use to reproduce games
items.excerpt: Unity's CEO says copying an existing game with AI doesn't make you an auteur, while launching Unity Spark, a prompt-based tool built to streamline AI-assisted game development.
items.note: Unity Spark launch itself already published (80.lv); this is the CEO-stance angle.

items.title: Wooga's Holger Wurst on designing June's Journey: Player research, AI and the UX rule you can't break
items.excerpt: Wooga's UI/UX lead on the $1B hidden-object game June's Journey, who runs 11 designers, animators and researchers, talks through AI's possibilities and limits for live-game UX and why player research still comes first.
items.note: off-list domain (pocketgamer.biz): design-org craft interview, no on-list equivalent

items.title: Google Play launches discoverability tool Game Finder using "gamer DNA"
items.excerpt: Google Play's Game Finder uses Google AI to build a "gamer DNA" profile from play habits, then recommends games by genre and mechanic. Players can also filter out titles that push in-app purchases.
items.note: off-list domain (pocketgamer.biz); no on-list coverage found

items.title: PlayStation Seeks To Solve Frame Generation's Number 1 Issue, As New Patent Details Frame Prediction Tech Slashing Input Delay
items.excerpt: A new Sony patent describes predicting future frames, instead of interpolating between them like ML frame generation, to cut input delay. It includes a non-AI fallback for wrong predictions.

items.title: A guide to six regulatory risks shaping games in 2026
items.excerpt: EU AI Act rules on deepfakes and on depicting real people and places in games have applied since August 2. Studios now have legal duties to disclose AI use, and generative-AI outputs must be marked as machine-detectable.
